questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Let air out faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let air out faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times lets air out of the brake system faster than the compressor can put it back.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine using gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to total stopping distance.

questions.question: Air lines should be securely connected to:
questions.explanation: When inspecting the converter dolly, make sure air lines are securely attached to the proper glad hands with no leaks. They should have enough slack to allow the vehicle to turn easily.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting your trip. On a vehicle with a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on.
questions.explanation: When air pressure falls below 60 psi, a low pressure warning signal activates. This signal appears as a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: Before a trip, the glide plate should be:

options.text: Far from the upper fifth wheel.
Securely mounted to the trailer frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Securely mounted to the trailer frame.
questions.explanation: Before starting your trip, inspect the upper fifth wheel. The glide plate must be securely mounted to the trailer frame.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Avoid using tricks to help them pass.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your distance from the vehicle ahead, avoid sudden movements, and avoid tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up is dangerous because it just makes the tailgater follow at a higher speed.

questions.question: When parking, you should:

options.text: Share a parking lot with automobiles.
Park where you can pull forward when leaving.
Ask drivers of smaller vehicles to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park where you can pull forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous and should be avoided. Choose a parking space that lets you pull forward when you leave. Avoid parking near smaller vehicles to prevent maneuvering problems.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer attached. Drivers must be extra careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: What can a trailer brake hand valve be used for on a truck?

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops a tractor-trailer from rolling backward when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a cargo fire in a box trailer?

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Cover the trailer with a large, heavy blanket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Never open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen and makes it bigger, especially if the cargo contains hazardous materials.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles have?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when traveling downhill?

options.text: It matches the speed of other traffic.

questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle faster when going downhill. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: What equipment must a CMV have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes a fire extinguisher, spare fuses, and three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three flares.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air brake leakage rate for a single vehicle in one minute?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle's air brake system should not leak more than 2 psi in one minute. If it does, do not drive the vehicle because it needs repair.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, what should you verify?

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pump, and fluid level. Look for leaks and fix them before driving.

questions.question: If you are turning left and there are two left turn lanes, which should you use?

options.text: Trucks should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra room to make left turns. Use the right lane when turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: Where water builds up on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water builds up on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water builds up on the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread make it more likely. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.
